findings.title: Test does not assert the behaviour it claims to cover
findings.rationale: The test name says 'scans using the registry default when no workspace override is saved', but the only assertion checks that the HTTP status is 202. A 202 response only means the request was accepted for processing; it does not confirm that the registry default model was used, that no error occurred during extraction, or that the extraction results are correct. If the production code had a bug where it used the wrong model or silently swallowed an error, this test would still pass. To guard the intended behaviour, the test should also assert on the response body (e.g., a job ID, extraction results, or a field indicating which model was used) or poll for the extraction outcome.

findings.title: Test does not verify the model actually used

It does not verify that the registry default model was selected for the extraction. If the production code silently used a hardcoded fallback or a different model, the test would still pass. To guard the intended behavior (using the registry default when no workspace override exists), the test should also assert something about the model used — for example, checking the response body for a model identifier or querying the database for the extraction record's model field.

findings.title: Test does not verify the extraction used the registry default model

findings.title: Test silently passes when Docker is unavailable
